extracted.intended_audience: educational institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for when and how recipients of federal education funds may permissively dismiss Title IX complaints under §106.45(d), including notification, appeal, and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of §106.45(d) to students
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient has discretion in how it communicates its obligations under §106.45(d) to students, including choice of terminology, so long as it effectively conveys the circumstances in which a recipient may decline to initiate or continue a Title IX investigation or grievance procedures and otherwise complies with §106.45(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the same terminology from final regulations may facilitate comparisons and enforcement, but recipients may use different wording appropriate to age, maturity, and educational level. Recipients are required to put grievance procedures in writing under §106.45(a)(1) and include information on how to locate them in the notice of nondiscrimination under §106.8(c)(1)(i)(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive dismissals (recipient discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.45(d)(1) permits, rather than requires, a recipient to dismiss a complaint in specified circumstances; recipients may either decline, initiate, or continue grievance procedures if any permissive dismissal reason is satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissive (not mandatory) dismissals support Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate by enabling investigations where further fact-finding may reveal sex discrimination. The Department concluded mandatory dismissal at the outset can limit Title IX enforcement and therefore grants recipient discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustive grounds for dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: The categories listed in §106.45(d)(1) are exhaustive; unless one of the four reasons under §106.45(d)(1) is satisfied, a recipient must implement grievance procedures under §106.45 (and as applicable §106.46) or an appropriate informal resolution process under §106.44(k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissals under §106.45(d)(1) are permissive; recipients cannot dismiss for reasons outside the enumerated categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(d)(1)(i) — Unable to identify the respondent
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may dismiss if it is unable to identify the respondent only after taking reasonable steps to identify the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable steps may include interviewing the complainant and potential witnesses and reviewing contemporaneous records (e.g., video footage, visitor logs). If identity cannot be ascertained, recipient should consider whether proceedings without a respondent would be effective (e.g., providing closure, addressing unsafe conditions, inadequate policies). A recipient may not dismiss a policy/practice sex discrimination complaint merely because no individual respondent is named.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(d)(1)(ii) — Respondent not participating or employed
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may permissively dismiss a complaint when the respondent is not participating in the recipient's education program or activity and is not employed by the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Participating’ is broader than mere enrollment (may include alumni, volunteers, attending events). Dismissal under this category is discretionary; recipients should consider whether the respondent poses ongoing risk, whether a determination would benefit the complainant, and obligations under other laws. If dismissal is elected, recipient must still offer supportive measures and take steps to prevent recurrence; recipient may choose to bar third parties from events or reopen the complaint if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(d)(1)(iii) — Complainant withdraws allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may permissively dismiss a complaint if the complainant voluntarily withdraws any or all of the allegations in the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether dismissal is appropriate is fact-specific: recipient must determine whether remaining allegations (if any) independently constitute sex discrimination. Even when allegations are withdrawn, §106.44(f)(1)(v) requires the Title IX Coordinator to consider whether other factors (e.g., imminent threat to health/safety) warrant initiating grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(d)(1)(iv) — Alleged conduct would not constitute sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may permissively dismiss a complaint if the alleged conduct, even if proven, would not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before dismissing under this provision, the recipient must make reasonable efforts to clarify the allegations with the complainant (to avoid dismissal based on limited English proficiency, disability, or misunderstanding). The Department declined to require mandatory dismissal of such complaints to avoid foregoing factfinding that might reveal sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dismissal based on credibility/factual determinations pre-investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient should not dismiss complaints on bases that depend on credibility assessments or factual determinations that require investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to add dismissal bases that would necessitate determining veracity without factfinding. For allegations such as retaliation, the proper response is to initiate an investigation under the recipient's grievance procedures rather than dismiss the underlying complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements for dismissal (§106.45(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient dismisses a complaint, it must notify the complainant and, as applicable, the respondent of the basis for the dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respondent must be notified of a dismissal only if the respondent had previously been notified of the allegations; notifying a respondent who had no prior notice could cause confusion or risk retaliation. Simultaneous notice to parties is required when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from a dismissal — availability and bases (§106.45(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer an appeal from a dismissed complaint on the same bases required under the 2020 amendments: procedural irregularity; new evidence not reasonably available at the time of dismissal; or bias or conflict of interest by the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations cross-reference these bases at §106.46(i)(1). Appeal availability for respondents is conditioned on whether the respondent had been notified of the complaint. The Department declined to require recipients to provide written appeal outcomes, though recipients may do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal process parity and applicability to K-12
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer an appeal process that is, at minimum, the same as it offers in comparable proceedings (if any), per §106.45(i); recipients must offer an appeal from a dismissal even if they do not generally offer appeals for final determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While elementary and secondary schools may not be required to offer appeals from final determinations in all cases, the Department views an appeal from dismissal as necessary because dismissal occurs before an investigation or determination is completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to offer supportive measures when dismissing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient dismisses a complaint under §106.45(d), it must offer supportive measures to the complainant and respondent, as appropriate, and take other prompt and effective steps to ensure sex discrimination does not continue or recur within the education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement (see §106.45(d)(4)(i) and (iii)) mitigates risk of depriving educational opportunity and complements any continuing obligations under other laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator role as resource
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator serves as a resource to complainants and respondents to explain grievance procedures and answer questions related to a recipient's procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because §106.45(d) may be confusing to complainants, the written grievance procedures and the Title IX Coordinator play a key role in ensuring parties understand when a recipient may decline to initiate or continue an investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and training requirements for officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person designated as a Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual party, and must be trained to serve impartially, including avoiding prejudgment of facts, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.45(b)(2) and §106.8(d)(2)(iii). The Department relied on these safeguards to rebut concerns that clarifying allegations with complainants would invite improper ex parte influence or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal does not eliminate other legal obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's permissive dismissal under Title IX does not relieve it of obligations under other laws (e.g., Title VII) that may require investigation and remediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when a complaint is dismissed under §106.45(d)(1), recipients may still have duties to investigate or address the conduct under other statutory or regulatory frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable efforts and remedial steps where respondent unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent cannot be identified, a recipient should consider remedial steps that do not depend on identifying an individual (e.g., denouncing conduct, convening assemblies, changing policies, offering counseling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cited Feminist Majority Foundation v. Hurley as an example where institutions should have taken broader steps to address anonymous harassment; dismissal is permitted under §106.45(d)(1)(i) only when such steps would be ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department technical assistance for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will offer technical assistance, as appropriate, to support recipients' implementation of the final regulations; the scope and timing will be determined in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should anticipate future guidance and assistance to help implement provisions such as how to investigate complaints by persons no longer participating in the education program or activity.
